title: I Took the Quilting-Frame Reservation to the Guild Lead Who Left Batting

parts.text: I unlocked frame A at 12:02 p.m. and lead Opal's batting was still taut on my unpaid-looking leftover. The calendar said: BOOK THE FRAME. THREE HOURS. STRIP THE BATTING. I was forty-two, guild member, holding a hold slip. Opal did not stop. "Leads are the frame." I photographed the calendar, the hold, and her pins on my time. Then I logged an overlap. At 12:09 the studio chair asked why Opal's batting was on my hold. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The studio chair can see Opal's batting on frame A during my reservation.

social.video_title: The guild lead left batting taut on my frame — Part 1/2
social.description: Quilting frame, a hold slip, batting still pinned. I logged the overlap. Would you have stripped it?

parts.text: Opal called it a sandwich until the chair asked for the log. I printed the overlap, the photo, and the slip. She stripped. Opal booked her own three hours and told members sandwiches were always about optics. Optics is a word leads use when pins exist. Reservation now has a second line: LEADS STRIP THE BATTING. I keep my three. Opal schedules. The frame finally looks like a hold, not leftover fluff. I kept the printout in a folder labeled BORING. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Overlap log, stripped frame, and a second line. Was a sandwich ever my hold?
